name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTH_MCQ_Q01 - Indeterminate growth and plant meristems

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding plant growth and meristems:

Statement I: Plants retain the capacity for unlimited growth throughout their life due to the presence of meristems at certain locations in their body.

Statement II: Root apical meristem and shoot apical meristem are responsible for secondary growth and cause an increase in the girth of the organs.

Statement III: The form of growth wherein new cells are always being added to the plant body by the activity of the meristem is called the open form of growth.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Plant growth is generally indeterminate because specific regions called meristems contain cells that divide and self-perpetuate, continuously adding new cells to the plant body.

Step 2: Evaluation of Unlimited Growth Capacity
The claim that plants retain the capacity for unlimited growth throughout their life due to meristems located at specific sites is accurate, as meristematic cells divide continuously while their derivatives differentiate into plant tissues.

Step 3: Evaluation of Apical Meristem Function
The claim that root apical meristem and shoot apical meristem cause secondary growth and an increase in girth is incorrect. Root and shoot apical meristems are responsible for primary growth, which contributes principally to the elongation of plants along their axis. Increase in girth (secondary growth) in dicotyledonous plants and gymnosperms is caused by lateral meristems, namely vascular cambium and cork-cambium.

Step 4: Evaluation of Open Form of Growth
The claim that continuous addition of new cells to the plant body by meristematic activity constitutes the open form of growth is accurate.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding unlimited growth due to meristems and the open form of growth are correct, whereas the claim attributing secondary growth in girth to apical meristems is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTH_MCQ_Q02 - Parameters used to measure plant growth

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the measurement of plant growth:

Statement I: Growth, at a cellular level, is principally a consequence of an increase in the amount of protoplasm.

Statement II: The growth of a pollen tube is measured in terms of its surface area, whereas an increase in length denotes the growth in a dorsiventral leaf.

Statement III: One single maize root apical meristem can give rise to more than 17,500 new cells per hour, expressing growth as an increase in cell number.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
At the cellular level, growth reflects an increase in protoplasm. Because protoplasmic increase is difficult to measure directly, proportional parameters such as fresh weight, dry weight, length, area, volume, and cell number are used.

Step 2: Evaluation of Cellular Basis of Growth
The claim that cellular growth is principally a consequence of an increase in the amount of protoplasm is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Measurement Parameters for Pollen Tube and Leaf
The claim regarding the measurement parameters for a pollen tube and a dorsiventral leaf is incorrect because the parameters are reversed. The growth of a pollen tube is measured in terms of its length, whereas an increase in surface area denotes the growth in a dorsiventral leaf.

Step 4: Evaluation of Maize Root Apical Meristem Cell Production
The claim that a single maize root apical meristem can produce more than 17,500 new cells per hour, representing growth as an increase in cell number, is accurate.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims concerning protoplasmic increase and cell number increase in a maize root apical meristem are correct, whereas the claim reversing the growth parameters of a pollen tube and a dorsiventral leaf is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTH_MCQ_Q03 - Characteristics of three phases of growth

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the phases of growth in a root tip:

Statement I: Cells in the meristematic phase are rich in protoplasm, possess large conspicuous nuclei, and have thin, primary cellulosic cell walls with abundant plasmodesmatal connections.

Statement II: Cells proximal to the meristematic zone represent the phase of elongation, characterised by increased vacuolation, cell enlargement, and new cell wall deposition.

Statement III: Cells in the phase of maturation lie closest to the root apex and continuously divide without undergoing wall thickening or protoplasmic modifications.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The period of growth in a plant axis is divided sequentially from the apex backwards into three phases: meristematic, elongation, and maturation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Meristematic Phase Characteristics
The claim describing meristematic cells as rich in protoplasm with large conspicuous nuclei and thin, primary cellulosic cell walls containing abundant plasmodesmatal connections is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Elongation Phase Characteristics
The claim that cells proximal (just next, away from the tip) to the meristematic zone represent the elongation phase and exhibit increased vacuolation, cell enlargement, and new cell wall deposition is accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of Maturation Phase Location and Features
The claim regarding the maturation phase is incorrect. Cells undergoing maturation lie further away from the apex (more proximal to the elongation zone), have lost the capacity for continuous division, and attain their maximal size in terms of wall thickening and protoplasmic modifications.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The descriptions of the meristematic phase and the elongation phase are correct, while the description placing the maturation phase closest to the apex without wall thickening is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTH_MCQ_Q04 - Arithmetic, geometric growth and relative growth rate

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding plant growth rates:

Statement I: In arithmetic growth, following mitotic cell division, only one daughter cell continues to divide while the other differentiates and matures, yielding a linear curve represented by \(L_t = L_0 + rt\).

Statement II: In geometric growth, both progeny cells retain the ability to divide, and under limited nutrient supply, plotting the growth parameter against time produces a typical sigmoid curve.

Statement III: If leaf A increases its area from \(5\text{ cm}^2\) to \(10\text{ cm}^2\) and leaf B increases its area from \(50\text{ cm}^2\) to \(55\text{ cm}^2\) in the same time interval, leaf B exhibits a higher relative growth rate than leaf A.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Leaf A grows from an initial area of \(5\text{ cm}^2\) to a final area of \(10\text{ cm}^2\). Leaf B grows from an initial area of \(50\text{ cm}^2\) to a final area of \(55\text{ cm}^2\) over the same time interval.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Absolute growth rate (AGR) is total growth per unit time, whereas relative growth rate (RGR) is growth per unit time expressed per unit initial parameter.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
For arithmetic growth, \(L_t = L_0 + rt\), where \(L_0\) is initial length, \(L_t\) is length at time \(t\), and \(r\) is elongation per unit time. For geometric growth under natural nutrient limits, the curve transitions from lag to log (exponential) and then stationary phase, forming a sigmoid (S) curve. Relative growth rate over a given interval is proportional to \(\frac{\text{Increase in area}}{\text{Initial area}} \times 100\%\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
First, the claim about arithmetic growth having only one dividing daughter cell and following \(L_t = L_0 + rt\) is accurate. Second, the claim about geometric growth producing a sigmoid curve under limited nutrient supply is accurate. Third, for the two leaves:
Absolute increase for Leaf A \(= 10\text{ cm}^2 - 5\text{ cm}^2 = 5\text{ cm}^2\).
Absolute increase for Leaf B \(= 55\text{ cm}^2 - 50\text{ cm}^2 = 5\text{ cm}^2\).
Relative percentage increase for Leaf A \(= \frac{5}{5} \times 100\% = 100\%\).
Relative percentage increase for Leaf B \(= \frac{5}{50} \times 100\% = 10\%\).
Because \(100\% > 10\%\), Leaf A exhibits a much higher relative growth rate than Leaf B, making the claim that Leaf B has a higher relative growth rate incorrect.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Both leaves have identical absolute growth (\(5\text{ cm}^2\)), but Leaf A starts from a smaller base (\(5\text{ cm}^2\)) and doubles in size, confirming its relative growth rate is higher. Thus, the claims regarding arithmetic growth and geometric sigmoid growth are correct, while the claim comparing the relative growth rates of the two leaves is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTH_MCQ_Q05 - Essential conditions required for plant growth

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the conditions necessary for plant growth:

Statement I: Plant cells grow in size by cell enlargement, which requires water because turgidity of cells helps in extension growth and water provides the medium for enzymatic activities.

Statement II: Oxygen helps in releasing metabolic energy essential for growth activities, while macro and micro essential nutrients are required for the synthesis of protoplasm and act as a source of energy.

Statement III: Any deviation from the optimum temperature range has no adverse effect on plant survival as long as water, oxygen, and nutrients are abundantly supplied.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Plant growth depends on essential internal and external factors including water, oxygen, nutrients, optimum temperature, and environmental signals like light and gravity.

Step 2: Evaluation of Role of Water
The claim that cell enlargement requires water for turgidity-driven extension growth and as a medium for enzymatic activities is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Role of Oxygen and Nutrients
The claim that oxygen helps release metabolic energy for growth and that macro and micro essential elements are required for protoplasm synthesis and as energy sources is accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of Temperature Range
The claim that deviation from the optimum temperature range has no adverse effect on survival when other resources are abundant is incorrect. Every plant organism has an optimum temperature range best suited for its growth, and any deviation from this range can be detrimental to its survival.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding the roles of water, oxygen, and nutrients are correct, whereas the claim dismissing the detrimental effect of temperature deviations is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTH_MCQ_Q06 - Differentiation, dedifferentiation, and open differentiation

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding differentiation in plants:

Statement I: During differentiation to form a tracheary element, cells lose their protoplasm and develop very strong, elastic, lignocellulosic secondary cell walls to carry water over long distances under extreme tension.

Statement II: The formation of meristems such as interfascicular cambium and cork cambium from fully differentiated parenchyma cells is an example of redifferentiation.

Statement III: Differentiation in plants is open because cells and tissues arising out of the same meristem can have different structures at maturity determined by their location within the plant.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cells derived from meristems mature to perform specific functions through differentiation. Living differentiated cells can regain division capacity via dedifferentiation, and their products can mature again via redifferentiation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Tracheary Element Differentiation
The claim that tracheary elements lose their protoplasm and develop strong, elastic, lignocellulosic secondary cell walls for long-distance water transport under tension is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Interfascicular and Cork Cambium Formation
The claim that forming interfascicular cambium and cork cambium from fully differentiated parenchyma cells is redifferentiation is incorrect. Regaining the capacity to divide by living differentiated cells is termed dedifferentiation. Redifferentiation occurs later when cells produced by these dedifferentiated meristems lose the ability to divide and mature for specific functions.

Step 4: Evaluation of Open Differentiation
The claim that differentiation in plants is open because the final structure at maturity of cells arising from the same meristem depends on cell location (for example, root-cap cells versus epidermis) is accurate.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding tracheary element differentiation and open differentiation are correct, whereas the claim misidentifying dedifferentiation as redifferentiation is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTH_MCQ_Q07 - Plant development and plasticity in heterophylly

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding development and plasticity in plants:

Statement I: Development is the sum of growth and differentiation, and includes all changes that an organism goes through during its life cycle from seed germination to senescence.

Statement II: Heterophylly in cotton, coriander, and larkspur represents plasticity in which the leaves of the juvenile plant differ in shape from those in mature plants.

Statement III: In buttercup, the difference in shapes of leaves produced in air and those produced in water represents heterophyllous development due to the environment.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Development encompasses the entire sequence of changes from seed germination to senescence and is the sum of growth and differentiation. Plasticity is the ability of plants to follow different developmental pathways in response to environmental conditions or phases of life.

Step 2: Evaluation of Definition of Development
The claim defining development as the sum of growth and differentiation spanning from germination to senescence is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Developmental Heterophylly
The claim that cotton, coriander, and larkspur exhibit plasticity through heterophylly, where juvenile leaves differ in shape from mature leaves, is accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of Environmental Heterophylly
The claim that buttercup exhibits heterophyllous development due to environmental differences between air (terrestrial) and water habitats is accurate.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
All three claims regarding the definition of development, developmental heterophylly in cotton, coriander, and larkspur, and environmental heterophylly in buttercup are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTH_MCQ_Q08 - Chemical nature and discovery of PGRs

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the chemical nature and discovery of plant growth regulators (PGRs):

Statement I: Indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) is an indole compound, kinetin is an adenine derivative, and abscisic acid (ABA) is a derivative of carotenoids.

Statement II: Charles Darwin and Francis Darwin observed phototropism in oat coleoptiles and isolated auxin from their tips.

Statement III: E. Kurosawa reported the appearance of 'bakanae' (foolish seedling) disease symptoms in rice seedlings treated with sterile filtrates of the fungus Gibberella fujikuroi, leading to the identification of gibberellic acid.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Plant growth regulators are small, simple molecules of diverse chemical compositions, and each of the five major groups was discovered through distinct experimental observations.

Step 2: Evaluation of Chemical Classification of PGRs
The claim that IAA is an indole compound, kinetin (\(N^6\)-furfurylamino purine) is an adenine derivative, and ABA is a carotenoid derivative is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Auxin Discovery
The claim regarding the Darwins' experiment is incorrect. Charles Darwin and Francis Darwin observed phototropism in the coleoptiles of canary grass (not oat) and concluded that the tip was the site of a transmittable influence. Auxin was later isolated by F.W. Went from the tips of coleoptiles of oat seedlings.

Step 4: Evaluation of Gibberellin Discovery
The claim that E. Kurosawa (1926) observed 'bakanae' disease symptoms in rice seedlings treated with sterile filtrates of Gibberella fujikuroi, with the active substance later identified as gibberellic acid, is accurate.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding the chemical nature of IAA, kinetin, and ABA, as well as Kurosawa's discovery of gibberellic acid, are correct, whereas the claim attributing oat coleoptile auxin isolation to the Darwins is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTH_MCQ_Q09 - Discovery of kinetin, abscisic acid, and ethylene

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the discovery of plant growth regulators:

Statement I: Miller et al. (1955) identified and crystallised a cytokinesis-promoting active substance and termed it kinetin.

Statement II: Inhibitor-B, abscission II, and dormin, purified independently during the mid-1960s, were later proved to be chemically identical and named abscisic acid (ABA).

Statement III: H.H. Cousins (1910) confirmed the release of a volatile substance from unripened bananas that hastened the ripening of stored oranges.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The discoveries of cytokinins, abscisic acid, and ethylene emerged from investigations into callus proliferation, growth inhibitors, and fruit ripening, respectively.

Step 2: Evaluation of Kinetin Discovery
The claim that Miller et al. (1955) identified and crystallised the cytokinesis-promoting active substance and termed it kinetin is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Abscisic Acid Discovery
The claim that inhibitor-B, abscission II, and dormin were purified independently during the mid-1960s and later shown to be chemically identical as abscisic acid (ABA) is accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of Ethylene Discovery
The claim regarding H.H. Cousins (1910) is incorrect because the direction of effect is reversed. Cousins confirmed the release of a volatile substance (later identified as ethylene) from ripened oranges that hastened the ripening of stored unripened bananas.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims concerning the discovery of kinetin and the chemical identity of ABA are correct, whereas the claim reversing the source and target fruits in Cousins' ethylene observation is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTH_MCQ_Q10 - Physiological effects and applications of auxins

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the physiological effects and applications of auxins:

Statement I: Synthetic auxins such as NAA and 2,4-D are used extensively in agricultural practices, with 2,4-D widely used to kill dicotyledonous weeds without affecting mature monocotyledonous plants.

Statement II: Auxins promote the abscission of young leaves and fruits at early stages, while preventing the abscission of older mature leaves and fruits.

Statement III: Removal of shoot tips (decapitation) overcomes apical dominance and results in the growth of lateral (axillary) buds, a practice widely applied in tea plantations and hedge-making.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Auxins (such as IAA, IBA, NAA, and 2,4-D) regulate diverse physiological processes including rooting, flowering, abscission, apical dominance, parthenocarpy, and xylem differentiation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Synthetic Auxin Herbicidal Action
The claim that NAA and 2,4-D are synthetic auxins used in agriculture, and that 2,4-D selectively kills dicotyledonous weeds without affecting mature monocotyledonous plants (such as lawn grasses), is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Auxin Effect on Abscission
The claim regarding abscission is incorrect because the effects on young and old organs are reversed. Auxins help prevent fruit and leaf drop at early stages, whereas they promote the abscission of older mature leaves and fruits.

Step 4: Evaluation of Apical Dominance and Decapitation
The claim that removing shoot tips (decapitation) removes the apical source of auxin, thereby overcoming apical dominance and promoting lateral bud growth in tea plantations and hedge-making, is accurate.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding synthetic auxins as selective herbicides and decapitation to overcome apical dominance are correct, while the claim reversing auxin's role in early versus mature organ abscission is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTH_MCQ_Q11 - Physiological roles of gibberellins and cytokinins

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding gibberellins and cytokinins:

Statement I: Gibberellic acid (\(\text{GA}_3\)) is used to speed up the malting process in the brewing industry, increase stem length and sugar yield in sugarcane, and promote bolting in rosette plants like beet and cabbages.

Statement II: Kinetin occurs naturally in higher plants and is synthesised in large amounts in root apices and developing shoot buds.

Statement III: Cytokinins help overcome apical dominance and promote nutrient mobilisation, which helps in the delay of leaf senescence.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Gibberellins and cytokinins are growth-promoting PGRs with distinct commercial and physiological roles in stem elongation, bolting, cell division, and senescence delay.

Step 2: Evaluation of Gibberellic Acid Applications
The claim that \(\text{GA}_3\) speeds up malting in the brewing industry, increases sugarcane stem length (boosting yield by up to 20 tonnes per acre), and promotes bolting (internode elongation prior to flowering) in beet and cabbages is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Natural Occurrence of Kinetin
The claim that kinetin occurs naturally in higher plants is incorrect. Kinetin (discovered from autoclaved herring sperm DNA) does not occur naturally in plants. Natural cytokinins (such as zeatin) are synthesised in regions of rapid cell division like root apices and developing shoot buds.

Step 4: Evaluation of Cytokinin Effects on Apical Dominance and Senescence
The claim that cytokinins help overcome apical dominance and promote nutrient mobilisation to delay leaf senescence is accurate.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding \(\text{GA}_3\) applications and cytokinin-mediated delay of senescence and release from apical dominance are correct, whereas the claim that kinetin occurs naturally in plants is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTH_MCQ_Q12 - Physiological effects of ethylene and ethephon

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding ethylene and its agricultural applications:

Statement I: Ethylene enhances the rate of respiration during fruit ripening, a phenomenon termed respiratory climactic, and promotes rapid internode or petiole elongation in deep water rice plants.

Statement II: Ethephon, an aqueous source of ethylene, hastens fruit ripening in tomatoes and apples, accelerates abscission in cotton, cherry, and walnut, and promotes female flowers in cucumbers.

Statement III: Ethylene induces seed and bud dormancy in peanut seeds and potato tubers, thereby preventing premature germination and sprouting.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Ethylene is a gaseous PGR that regulates fruit ripening, senescence, abscission, elongation in submerged rice, flowering, and dormancy breaking. Ethephon is the most widely used agricultural source of ethylene.

Step 2: Evaluation of Respiratory Climactic and Deep Water Rice
The claim that ethylene causes respiratory climactic (enhanced respiration rate during fruit ripening) and promotes rapid internode or petiole elongation in deep water rice plants (keeping leaves above water) is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Ethephon Applications
The claim that ethephon hastens ripening in tomatoes and apples, accelerates abscission (thinning) in cotton, cherry, and walnut, and promotes female flowers in cucumbers to increase yield is accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of Ethylene Effect on Dormancy
The claim that ethylene induces seed and bud dormancy in peanut seeds and potato tubers is incorrect. Ethylene actually breaks seed and bud dormancy, initiating germination in peanut seeds and sprouting of potato tubers.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding respiratory climactic, deep water rice elongation, and ethephon applications are correct, whereas the claim that ethylene induces dormancy in peanut seeds and potato tubers is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTH_MCQ_Q13 - Abscisic acid as stress hormone and GA antagonist

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding abscisic acid (ABA):

Statement I: ABA stimulates the closure of stomata and increases the tolerance of plants to various kinds of stresses, earning it the name 'stress hormone'.

Statement II: By inducing seed dormancy, ABA helps seeds withstand desiccation and other factors unfavourable for growth.

Statement III: In most physiological situations, ABA acts synergistically with gibberellins (GAs) to promote seed germination.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Abscisic acid (ABA) acts as a general plant growth and metabolism inhibitor that plays a major role in stress tolerance, stomatal regulation, and seed dormancy.

Step 2: Evaluation of Stress Hormone Role
The claim that ABA stimulates stomatal closure and enhances plant tolerance to various stresses, and is therefore called the stress hormone, is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Role in Seed Dormancy
The claim that ABA induces seed dormancy to help seeds withstand desiccation and unfavourable growth conditions is accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of Interaction with Gibberellins
The claim that ABA acts synergistically with gibberellins to promote seed germination is incorrect. ABA inhibits seed germination and acts as an antagonist to gibberellins in most situations.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding ABA's role as a stress hormone and its induction of seed dormancy against desiccation are correct, whereas the claim describing ABA as synergistic with gibberellins in promoting germination is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTH_MCQ_Q14 - Photoperiodism, dark period, and site of perception

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding photoperiodism in plants:

Statement I: Long day plants require exposure to light for a period exceeding a well-defined critical duration, whereas short day plants must be exposed to light for a period less than this critical duration before flowering is initiated.

Statement II: Flowering in photoperiodic plants depends solely on the duration of the light period, while the duration of the dark period plays no role in inducing flowering.

Statement III: The site of perception of light/dark duration is the leaves, from which a hypothesised hormonal substance migrates to the shoot apices to induce flowering.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Photoperiodism is the flowering response of plants to the relative durations of light and dark periods, perceived by the leaves and transmitted to the shoot apices.

Step 2: Evaluation of Long Day and Short Day Definitions
The claim defining long day plants as requiring light exposure exceeding a critical duration and short day plants as requiring light exposure less than the critical duration is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Role of Dark Period
The claim that flowering depends solely on the light period and that the dark period plays no role is incorrect. Both the duration of the light period and the duration of the dark period are of equal importance; flowering depends on the combination of light and dark exposures and their relative durations.

Step 4: Evaluation of Site of Perception
The claim that leaves are the site of perception of light/dark duration and that a hypothesised hormonal substance migrates from leaves to shoot apices to induce flowering is accurate.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims defining long day and short day plants and identifying leaves as the site of photoperiod perception are correct, whereas the claim dismissing the importance of the dark period is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTH_MCQ_Q15 - Vernalisation and methods to overcome seed dormancy

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding vernalisation and seed dormancy:

Statement I: Vernalisation refers to the promotion of flowering by a period of low temperature, which prevents precocious reproductive development late in the growing season.

Statement II: Winter varieties of wheat, barley, and rye are normally planted in spring so that they flower and produce mature grain before the end of the same flowering season.

Statement III: Seed dormancy caused by hard seed coats or chemical inhibitors like abscisic acid can be overcome by mechanical abrasions, chilling conditions, or application of gibberellic acid and nitrates.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Vernalisation is low-temperature promotion of flowering, while seed dormancy is an endogenous block to germination even under favourable external conditions.

Step 2: Evaluation of Vernalisation Significance
The claim that vernalisation promotes flowering through low-temperature exposure and prevents precocious reproductive development late in the growing season is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Winter Varieties Planting Season
The claim that winter varieties of wheat, barley, and rye are planted in spring to flower within the same season is incorrect. It is the spring varieties that are planted in spring. Winter varieties, if planted in spring, fail to flower or produce mature grain within a single flowering season; hence, they are planted in autumn, overwinter as small seedlings, resume growth in spring, and are harvested around mid-summer.

Step 4: Evaluation of Breaking Seed Dormancy
The claim that seed dormancy from hard seed coats or chemical inhibitors can be overcome by mechanical abrasions, chilling conditions, or application of gibberellic acid and nitrates is accurate.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding the significance of vernalisation and the methods to overcome seed dormancy are correct, whereas the claim about planting winter cereal varieties in spring is incorrect.
